title: It
scene: Early-1980s Sheffield indie pop / pastoral British folk
notes: Mostly acoustic pastoral mini-LP, with restrained drums and gentle early storytelling.

title: Freaks
scene: 1980s Sheffield art-damaged post-punk and gothic indie
notes: Gloomy outsider portraits over murky guitars, Farfisa organ, violin and theatrical vocals.

title: Separations
scene: Sheffield independent pop meets late-1980s acid-house and disco
sounds_like: Soft Cell|Scott Walker|The Human League|Marc Almond
notes: Side one broods; side two discovers drum-machine disco, sampling and Cocker’s intimate monologues.

title: His 'n' Hers
scene: 1994 Sheffield/London Britpop, glam and analogue-keyboard pop
sounds_like: David Bowie|Roxy Music|Suede|Soft Cell|The Human League
notes: Lurid, witty relationship dramas entwine retro synthesizers, glam guitars and restless narrative delivery.

title: Different Class
scene: Mid-1990s British Britpop / Sheffield social-realist synth-and-guitar pop
sounds_like: Suede|David Bowie|Roxy Music|The Human League|Blur|The Kinks
notes: Class satire and erotic stories erupt through propulsive synth-pop, guitars and cinematic orchestration.

title: This Is Hardcore
scene: Late Britpop backlash / ornate, decaying British art-rock
sounds_like: Scott Walker|David Bowie|Roxy Music|The Divine Comedy|Leonard Cohen
notes: Dark cinematic art rock confronts fame, age, lust and failure with dramatic strings.

title: We Love Life
scene: Early-2000s British art-rock and orchestral post-Britpop
sounds_like: Scott Walker|The Divine Comedy|Richard Hawley|Roxy Music
notes: Walker-guided acoustic and orchestral songs turn outsider anxieties toward nature, memory and renewal.

title: More
scene: Contemporary UK art-rock revival / post-Britpop and orchestral pop
sounds_like: Scott Walker|David Bowie|The Last Shadow Puppets|Roxy Music|Richard Hawley
notes: Adult intimacy and mortality meet sumptuous strings, measured disco grooves and witty theatrical vocals.
